source.quote: Naim Audio's own product page for the ND5 XS 2, read 2026-11-24. Inputs: « 1 x coaxial RCA (up to 24bit/192kHz, DoP 64Fs) », « 1 x coaxial BNC (up to 24bit/192kHz, DoP 64Fs) », « 2 x optical TOSLink (up to 24bit/96kHz) ». Technology: « decoding all HD audio formats at up to 32 bits/384 kHz or DSD128 ». Audio Formats: « DSD - 64 and 128Fs ». Conversion: « the data is oversampled in a SHARC DSP with 40-bit accuracy before being fed to the PCM1791A Burr-Brown digital-to-analogue converter. » Product type: « Streamer ».

facts.chip: PCM1791A, named by the maker as « the PCM1791A Burr-Brown digital-to-analogue converter ». The same page states what precedes it: « the data is oversampled in a SHARC DSP with 40-bit accuracy before being fed to » the converter - a maker saying in its own words that a DSP stage sits in the path.

_optical_at_96: Another optical input rated at 96 kHz by its maker, not 192. That is the fourth record here to confirm the catalogue's conservative optical default rather than contradict it - see vocabulary/why-the-optical-default-stays-low.
_what_is_not_asserted: NO NETWORK INPUT IS CLAIMED. The 384 kHz and DSD128 figures are stated for decoding in general, not for a named protocol, and this catalogue has six distinct network interfaces - asserting one of them from a sentence that names none would be inventing the subject. They are recorded at DEVICE level, where the source puts them. No USB input either: the page says « It also has digital and USB inputs » and gives no USB row in the specification list, so there is nothing to assert. dsd_direct is NOT inferred from the SHARC sentence: that a DSP oversamples PCM says nothing certain about what happens to DSD, and guessing it is how this catalogue got its worst records.
_a_contradiction_inside_the_source: The features prose says « It has two digital inputs and two optical inputs » while the specification rows list two COAXIAL inputs (RCA and BNC) plus two optical. The rows are the more specific statement and are what is recorded. Worth knowing that a maker's own page can disagree with itself.
_discontinued: Naim's own page says « This product is no longer available », and the category page lists it under « Discontinued products ». It is still documented, which is why this record exists at all - and it is the third device in this pass whose installed base outlives its catalogue entry, after eversolo DMP-A6 and the Denafrips Terminator II that Denafrips no longer lists.
